Use Brisk-S few-shot for the turn router: it is the only configuration inside the overall accuracy, cell floor and latency gates at once.

It clears overall accuracy with its whole interval and its weakest cell, complex news, by 2.9 points. The call would change if its p95 latency, measured only as a point estimate, ran over budget, or if the far cheaper Nano-XS few-shot were fixed on complex news.

!
Confidence: High, if the caveats below aren't material.
  • Latency budget (p95) is cleared on a point estimate. Only if the true p95 of Brisk-S few-shot is over the budget: it reads 184 ms against 250 ms with no interval, so nothing says how much of the 66 ms clearance is noise. Accuracy, the other two gates, is measured with intervals clear of its lines.
  • The pick is the best of several candidates. Only if the pick's thinnest clearance re-reads below its line on fresh cases: chosen from 9 configurations, its figures read somewhat high, but its overall interval (90.4–91%) and its complex-news cell both sit clear of their lines today.
  • No arm is the control. Only for claims that one configuration beats another: those read each arm's own spread, unpaired and so wide. The call itself rests on each configuration against the declared gates, which needs no control.
RecommendationRoute turns with Brisk-S few-shot. It passes every declared gate, at $1,200.00 a month at the declared volume.
Why not the othersNano-XS few-shot is cheaper but misses the complex-news floor at 76.7%, its whole interval below the line. Brisk-S rubric, Atlas-M few-shot and Atlas-M rubric are more accurate but break the latency budget; Brisk-S rubric reads 496 ms. Atlas-M zero-shot breaks the budget and misses overall accuracy too, and the remaining configurations miss overall accuracy.
WatchLatency is the least-evidenced gate: a point estimate with no interval. Complex news is the thinnest accuracy clearance, though a fresh run of today's size would almost never read it below the floor (0.0001087%). Picked as the one of 9 that passes, its figures likely read a little high on a rerun.

What you could change

What you could changeWhat it decidesWhat happens as it moves
Cell floorWhich configuration passes every cellBelow 76.7%, Nano-XS few-shot passes and, being cheapest, becomes the pick. From there up to 82.9%, Brisk-S few-shot holds. Above that, no configuration passes.
Overall accuracy lineWhich configurations pass overallBrisk-S few-shot holds at any line up to 90.7%; lowering the line admits no cheaper option, since each also fails the cell floor or the budget. Above it, nothing passes.
Latency budgetWhich configurations pass on latencyBelow 184 ms, nothing passes. Any budget above it keeps Brisk-S few-shot; a much looser one admits more accurate but costlier configurations, such as Brisk-S rubric, gaining +0.8 points, which would then be a price to weigh.

Next steps

  • Re-measure Brisk-S few-shot's p95 latency with an interval, under production-like load. Whether the latency clearance is real, turning the open latency caveat into evidence or reopening the choice.
  • Add complex-news examples to Nano-XS few-shot's prompt and re-run that cell; more cases alone would not help, since its interval already sits below the floor. Whether a configuration at a fraction of the pick's cost can pass every gate; if it does, it replaces the pick.
  • Re-run Brisk-S few-shot on a fresh held-out sample of complex news turns. Whether the pick's thinnest accuracy clearance survives the optimism of picking the best of many.

Method

Cases
48210 turns per configuration, the same turns for each, run once; complex news holds 3600 of them.
Accuracy
In a cell, the share of turns whose true complexity and domain fall in that cell that the router labels correctly. Balanced accuracy is the plain mean of the nine cells' accuracies.
Gates
Balanced accuracy at least 90%; accuracy in every cell at least 80%; p95 latency at most 250 ms. No criterion is marked as set after the results. Accuracy gates are read on the whole interval where one exists, latency on its point estimate.
Intervals
Cell accuracies carry intervals as stated, at 95%. The interval on balanced accuracy is derived from the cells', read as independent. Comparisons between configurations combine each one's own spread as if independent, so they read wider than paired ones; no multiplicity correction applies to them, and they are descriptive.
Control
None: nine configurations, three models crossed with three prompts, compared on equal footing.

Caveats: No arm is the control.

Cost
Cost per million turns as measured, priced at the declared 30000000 turns a month.
Source
Turn router classifier sweep, synthetic example data.

Review findings left open

  • Must fix · Claim 2: c2 says the pick's thinnest clearance is complex news (82.9%, 2.9 points above the floor). The thinnest is actually overall balanced accuracy: 90.7% against 90%, a gap of 0.7 points (criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap), with the interval's low end at 90.4%. The chance of a fresh run reading it on the wrong side is also higher than for complex news (0.0004972% against 0.0001087%). Fix: say complex news is the weakest cell, and name overall accuracy as the thinnest gate clearance.
  • Must fix · The page: Watch and the lede treat complex news as the accuracy risk and never mention the 0.7-point overall margin, the pick's weakest margin on any gate (the computed fact weakest_not_in_watch). Sweeping the overall line shows the call disappears above 90.7%, and a best-of-9 pick reads high by chance. Fix: add a Watch entry citing the overall value, line and gap (criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.value, .low, .gap), and name it in the lede next to the latency risk.
  • Should fix · The page: The third next step reruns only complex news to test best-of-9 optimism. Extend it to a full fresh held-out run, so it also re-reads overall balanced accuracy, the clearance most at risk.
  • Should fix · The page: Nano-XS few-shot's overall accuracy is borderline: 90.1%, interval 89.8–90.4% (criteria.overall.nano-xs.few.low/high). Yet 'Why not the others', the Nano-XS next step ('passes every gate') and the cell-floor row in 'What you could change' ('Nano-XS few-shot passes') treat it as clearing overall. Say it is borderline overall. Then make the Nano-XS next step settle both the complex-news floor and the overall line, perhaps noting that fixing complex news would also raise its balanced accuracy.
  • Should fix · Claim 3: The difference table's caption says each row is 'overall and in each place', but the table has no overall row. Add Brisk-S few-shot minus Nano-XS few-shot on balanced accuracy, or drop 'overall' from the caption.
